items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I think that Doc deserves a lot of the credit for doing that. He told me that he was afraid that they wouldn't get anything done on the date... Bix played one of his best choruses, and the saxophone chorus was terrific.

ctx.x: So he would be around and he would, I guess he took the orchestration and told Trumbauer to get his saxophone thing, work out a saxophone chorus and then it would give -- well, Bix didn't have -- tell them to woodshed, we had a term then go over in your corner and woodshed these parts and then we'd come back and put the whole thing together.
Now, I think that Doc deserves a lot of the credit for doing that. He told me that he was afraid that they wouldn't get anything done on the date. I think it was down

in Camden that that was made.
Anyway, it turned out fine. Bix played one of his best choruses, and the saxophone chorus was terrific. So I went around to the Paramount and got in touch with Whiteman and he said, 'Okay, we go up to Boston and so be there and go up with us,' so he said, 'Don't worry about doing any arrangements; just get acquainted with the guys in the band and what we do.'
